Krapfen

Served at: Perchta Day (Perchtenlauf)

Makes about 12 KrapfenPrep 30 minCook 15 min

Krapfen are traditional Austrian and Bavarian fried pastries, similar to doughnuts, often filled with jam or custard. They are a festive treat commonly enjoyed during Perchta Day (Perchtenlauf), a winter holiday celebrating the Alpine goddess Perchta, where these sweet treats symbolize warmth and good fortune for the coming year.

Ingredients

  • 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast (1 packet)
  • 1/4 cup warm milk (60 ml)
  • 3 cups all-purpose flour (375 g)
  • 1/4 cup granulated sugar (50 g)
  • 1/4 tsp salt
  • 3 large egg yolks
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened (113 g)
  • 1/2 cup sour cream (120 ml)
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • Vegetable oil for frying
  • 1 cup apricot jam (or preferred jam) (320 g)
  • Powdered sugar for dusting

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve the yeast in warm milk and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
  2. In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, and salt.
  3. Add the egg yolks, softened butter, sour cream, vanilla extract, and the yeast mixture to the dry ingredients.
  4. Mix until a soft dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  5. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a clean towel, and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour or until doubled in size.
  6. Punch down the dough and roll it out to about 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) thickness.
  7. Cut out 3-inch (7.5 cm) circles using a cookie cutter or glass.
  8. Place the circles on a floured surface, cover, and let them rise for another 30 minutes.
  9. Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 350°F (175°C).
  10. Fry the dough circles in batches, about 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown.
  11. Drain on paper towels and let cool slightly.
  12. Using a pastry bag fitted with a small tip, fill each Krapfen with apricot jam by inserting the tip into the side and gently squeezing.
  13. Dust the filled Krapfen generously with powdered sugar before serving.

Tips

  • Ensure the milk is warm, not hot, to activate the yeast properly without killing it.
  • For a richer filling, substitute apricot jam with vanilla custard or chocolate spread.
  • Serve Krapfen fresh the same day for the best texture and flavor.
